package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to Android 10 (at least up to 1.1)
package_info.why_malicious: The package exposes an exported activity (TagViewer) without permission protection, allowing any app to trigger it via crafted intents. This enables malicious apps to spoof NFC tag reads and present attacker-controlled content to users, facilitating phishing, social engineering, or redirection attacks by abusing system trust in NFC events.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a malicious app sends a crafted intent to the TagViewer activity
execution_context.file_location: com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer (exported activity, accessible via explicit intent)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code constructs a fake NDEF message containing a URI, creates an explicit intent targeting the TagViewer activity, injects the crafted NDEF message as an extra, and launches the activity, resulting in the system displaying a 'new tag scanned' popup with attacker-controlled content.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code enables any app to simulate an NFC tag scan and present arbitrary data to the user by directly invoking a system UI component, bypassing the expected hardware-based NFC event.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, only genuine NFC hardware events should trigger the TagViewer activity, ensuring that tag content is authentic. Here, any app can programmatically trigger the UI, breaking the trust boundary between system and user.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use may occur in development or testing environments where NFC events are simulated, but in production, apps should not be able to spoof user-facing system dialogs or inject arbitrary tag data.
key_indicators: Exported activity (TagViewer) with no permission protection
Explicit intent sent to com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer with NDEF message extras
Ability to inject arbitrary NDEF messages to system UI
Triggering 'new tag scanned' dialogs without actual NFC hardware events

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a malicious app intercepts a real NFC scan via intent filter
execution_context.file_location: Malicious app's AndroidManifest.xml (intent filter for android.nfc.action.NDEF_DISCOVERED) and app code handling onNewIntent

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malicious app registers for NFC tag intents, intercepts a real NFC scan, reads and modifies the tag content (such as changing a phone number or URL), and then relaunches the TagViewer activity with the spoofed data, causing the user to see altered content as if it were genuine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and modifying NFC tag data before it reaches the system handler constitutes a man-in-the-middle attack, allowing the attacker to alter what the user sees and potentially redirect actions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Users expect the system to present NFC tag content as read from the physical tag, not altered by third-party apps. This breaks the integrity of the NFC data flow.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Debugging or development tools may intercept and modify NFC intents for testing, but such behavior is not expected in production apps or without explicit user consent.
key_indicators: Intent filter for android.nfc.action.NDEF_DISCOVERED in AndroidManifest.xml
App code handling onNewIntent to modify and forward NDEF messages
Forwarding spoofed NDEF data to com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer
On-the-fly modification of NFC tag data before user presentation

attack_chain.action: Malicious app registers for NFC intents (e.g., NDEF_DISCOVERED) to intercept tag scans or crafts a fake intent to simulate a tag scan, exploiting the exported TagViewer activity.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is presented with a spoofed 'new tag scanned' dialog containing attacker-controlled data.

attack_chain.action: User interacts with the spoofed tag content (such as clicking a malicious link, calling a manipulated phone number, or sending an SMS), believing it to be genuine system-presented data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential phishing, social engineering, or redirection to attacker-controlled resources.

behavioral_signatures: Apps sending explicit intents to com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer with crafted NDEF messages, especially without a corresponding NFC hardware event
Apps registering for android.nfc.action.NDEF_DISCOVERED and relaunching TagViewer with modified or attacker-controlled data
Unexpected 'new tag scanned' popups occurring without actual NFC hardware activity
file_indicators: App code invoking startActivity with com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer as the target component and NDEF message extras
network_indicators: NDEF messages containing suspicious or known phishing URLs (e.g., http://kripthor.com/nfc)
Redirection to attacker-controlled phone numbers or SMS endpoints embedded in NDEF records
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps that send explicit intents to com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer with NDEF message extras, particularly when no NFC hardware event is detected. Flag apps that register for high-priority NFC intent filters and modify or forward tag data to system UI components. Alert on repeated or unexpected 'new tag scanned' dialogs, especially if the device's NFC hardware was not activated. Correlate NDEF message content with known malicious domains, phone numbers, or SMS endpoints.
